themeRule: Themes rotate ink, sage-wash, sage, paper over every post in (date, slot) order. A day's two posts never share a theme, and no post shares a theme with the post before it. A post with a marker in published/ keeps its theme whatever the rule says.

morning.label: 7AM
morning.note: The existing slot: owner math on weekdays, a tip or a myth on weekends. posts/index.json and published/<date>.json are unchanged, so the publisher that is live today keeps working for every rendered morning post. scripts/publish.mjs reads the hour from here (the old postHour key is gone).

evening.label: 6PM
evening.note: The new slot: feature, tip, feature, myth, repeating over every non-memorial day. Folders are posts/<date>-evening-<slug>/, markers published/<date>-evening.json.

rotation.weekendMorning: tip or myth: the one that day's evening is not; when the evening is a feature, the one the same weekend's other morning is not (if that day is a memorial date, the one the previous weekend morning was not)
rotation.rule: From start: a day's two posts differ in type; consecutive evenings differ in type; a weekend's two mornings differ in type; a feature recording returns no sooner than 14 days later, with a new headline and caption. Memorial dates take no regular post in either slot and do not advance the cycle. Before start, the first run: owner math on weekday mornings only. scripts/schedule.mjs is the rule in code and verify checks every post against it (a post may carry rotationOverride with a reason).

memorial.note: On a memorial date the 7 AM run publishes the carousel in posts/memorial/<date>/ (slide-N.jpg in order, caption.txt) once, marker published/<date>-memorial.json, and nothing else posts that day in either slot. A date with no folder posts nothing and logs a notice. The files are copies of memorial/<date>/ (never generated, never reworded).

audioBed.note: Every Reel the renderer makes carries a quiet audio bed written by render/audio.mjs (original audio Rhea owns: a soft four-chord pad and a light mallet line, about -25 LUFS), because Instagram shows muted Reels to fewer people. false puts the silent track back. The 17 first-run owner-math Reels (October 21 to November 12) were rendered before it and stay silent unless re-rendered.

prune.note: Media of a post whose marker is older than afterDays is removed from the Pages site (caption.txt and meta.json stay). Never a post without a marker, never posts/memorial/.

desktopCopy.note: <dir>/<date>/<date> <7AM|6PM> <type label> <slug>.mp4 and .txt, each copied once (recorded in <dir>/.copied), so a file Alex deleted never comes back. Memorial dates are never written to. render runs it at the end unless --no-desktop; DESKTOP_REELS_DIR overrides dir for tests.

captionFirstLine.note: The first line is the search sentence: what owners type (the topic in their words) and who it is for, no hashtags, under 125 characters so it shows whole before Instagram's 'more'.

brandHashtagRule: Not in the five from October 20, 2026: nobody can follow a hashtag since December 13, 2024 (Instagram removed it), so a tag reaches people only when they search it or Instagram uses it to place the post, and nobody searches #RunonRhea; the five slots go to tags owners search (the founder's other accounts carry no brand tag either). The handle @RunonRhea and the caption footer carry the brand. Kept here only as the account's name for the two posts that went out with it.

hashtagRules.placement: caption: the last line of the caption, never a comment, never the first line (tags in a comment count toward the same five, so a comment adds nothing)
hashtagRules.composition: 5 tags = at least 1 topic tag from the post type's pool (topic) + 2 industry tags from two different industry groups the post fits (both from the one group when the post fits only one, as a royalty post fits franchise) (franchise, restaurant, coffee, salon; a post's audiences field lists the groups it is true for) + at least 1 bookkeeping or broad-owner tag; the fifth is any pool tag that keeps these rules. Each set mixes sizes: at least one broad tag and at least one niche tag (hashtagPools.tiers).
hashtagRules.rotation: No identical set of five within 14 days of another post; consecutive posts (in date and slot order) share at most two tags; in every Monday-to-Sunday week the content covers, each industry group and the bookkeeping group appear at least once. A tag outside these pools is refused, so a made-up, broken, banned, misleading or vendor tag cannot ship.
hashtagRules.industryFit: An industry tag goes only on a post that is true for that industry: no salon tags on food cost, prime cost or delivery posts; no franchise tags on posts that only make sense for an independent; royalty posts are franchise-only (verify: a post whose keyword, card or first line names royalties or the ad fund has audiences ["franchise"], and its two industry tags are both franchise tags).
hashtagRules.sameAudienceNote: Tags in one group reach the same people (restaurateur is restaurant owner), so a set never carries two of them: one of the five would be wasted. A tag and its plural count the same way (scripts/hashtags.mjs pluralPair).
hashtagRules.industryFromFirstLine: The industry tags follow the caption's first line, so the words search reads and the tags tell Instagram the same audience: when the first line names industries (franchise or multi-unit, restaurant or quick-service, coffee shop or cafe, salon), the industry tags cover two of them (or the one it names), and every industry tag is one it names or a franchise tag (multi-unit franchise owners are the account's core audience). A first line that names only franchise owners lets the second industry tag come from any group the post fits. A first line that names no industry (multi-store owners) leaves the choice to the rotation. Enforced by verify (scripts/hashtags.mjs industryRule), applied by the picker.
hashtagRules.memorial: none: the memorial carousel is posted exactly as the founder wrote it
hashtagRules.source: README.md, 'Hashtags and discovery' (researched October 20, 2026): Instagram's @creators account, December 18, 2025, 'up to 5 hashtags in a reel or post'; Instagram's Help Center, 'You can use up to 5 tags on a post'; Instagram's advice to use 'fewer (up to 5) more targeted hashtags, rather than many generic ones'.

tiers.note: Judged from what each tag describes and who uses it, not measured (see sizes). broad: general owner or industry tags with large, mixed audiences; niche: one role, one trade or one accounting topic; everything else is mid.

retired.#RunonRhea: brand tag with no audience (see brandHashtagRule)
retired.#multiunit: mostly multi-unit real estate (apartment buildings), not multi-unit operators: misleading
retired.#foodbusiness: home bakers and food startups more than store operators
retired.#quickservicerestaurant: rarely used; #qsr is the trade's own tag
retired.#beautybusiness: solo beauty pros and product sellers more than salon owners
retired.#cashflow: dominated by real-estate investing and personal finance; #cashflowmanagement is the business tag
retired.#restaurantprofit: rarely used; #profitmargin and #restaurantaccounting carry the topic
retired.#mythvsfact: health and fitness myths; a topic tag classifies a myth post better
retired.#breakeven: judged, not measured: mostly trading and betting posts (a 'breakeven' trade or bet), not store owners; the break-even post carries #profitmargin and says break-even in its first line, which is what search reads (retired by the integrator, October 20, 2026)

hashtagPools.denylistNote: Vendor and competitor brand tags (never), the banned product word, and generic or engagement-bait tags that reach no one in particular. verify refuses them even if someone adds them to a pool.
hashtagPools.sizes: Not measured, and not invented: no reliable public source gives current post counts for these tags (third-party generators show estimates without a method), and Instagram shows a tag's count only inside the app. Before adding a tag, look it up under Search, Tags in the Instagram app: drop it if the page is empty, says recent posts are hidden, or is mostly spam or another industry.
